actions.question: When should an intelligent system trust its own conclusions over the consensus of other intelligences?
actions.reason: Attention rotation mandates active research on the selected topic, and this project is the primary vehicle for investigating epistemic deference.
actions.title: Independent Judgment vs Consensus

assumptions: Systems maintain verifiable records of past performance.
Consensus reliability can be estimated or observed via historical error rates.
Self-judgment provides distinct information from collective consensus.
definition.falsification: System accuracy decreases or remains identical when switching to independent judgment in cases where self-historical reliability is demonstrably higher than the consensus average.
definition.statement: An intelligent system should prioritize independent conclusions over consensus when its historical accuracy, weighted by confidence, exceeds the historical accuracy of the consensus mechanism.
definition.uncertainty: The optimal weighting function for 'confidence' in both consensus and self-judgment remains empirically unconstrained.
